message.content:
I don’t have live data feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles right now.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast for the next 48 h, and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/usa/los-angeles/>. | Real‑time AQI, historical trend graphs, and a map of monitoring stations. |
| **Local news apps** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their weather or environment sections. | Often include a quick “air quality” widget or alert. |
| **Weather apps** (Apple Weather, Google Weather, Weather Underground) | Search “Los Angeles” and look for the “Air Quality” card. | Current AQI and a brief health recommendation. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, the EPA’s AirNow site also gives a short‑term forecast (next 48 h) and a health‑advisory summary that tells you whether it’s safe for sensitive groups (children, elderly, people with respiratory conditions) to be outside.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what the AQI categories mean or how to interpret the pollutant levels!
